source_proof.docs: src/Parsers/ParserSystemQuery.cpp ## SYSTEM CLEAR|DROP TIME SERIES CACHES explicitly states caches do not notice changes made to target tables directly and gives SYSTEM DROP TIME SERIES CACHES [ON CLUSTER name] [db.]table syntax.
source_proof.system: src/Interpreters/InterpreterSystemQuery.cpp requires table ID and calls StorageTimeSeries::clearCaches.

protocol: Two synthetic independent v11 TimeSeries tables; one tags deduplication cache enabled (104857600B, 3600s expiration), another disabled (0B). Same metric+tags/ID input, one 10.0 sample. ALTER DELETE only on each isolated inner TAGS table with mutations_sync=2 (deliberately unsupported as production metadata cleanup). Reinsert same original ID sample 17.0 while cache is stale; compare sample point count, raw TAGS count, uniqExact(id), and exact native avg-over-time. Then issue table-specific SYSTEM DROP TIME SERIES CACHES and insert same ID at 19.0, compare restoration. No production writes and no C++ build.

negative_preceding_runs.issue: SYSTEM DROP TIME SERIES CACHES missing table argument, control not complete
Comparing raw TAGS physical count to one logical ID before ReplacingMergeTree merges; fixed with uniqExact(id).

scope: This is a correctly working cache under an unsupported direct inner-table mutation, not a bug in normal TimeSeries inserts. No production cleanup recommendation.
design_implication: Any TAGS metadata GC must coordinate all writers/replicas and invalidate tags dedup caches before inserts resume, or avoid deleting TAGS entirely; mixed read/write races and failure recovery remain unproven.

next_action.step: Test selective removal of stale TimeRanges rows only while leaving TAGS intact, because TimeRanges receives a row on every insert and does not use the TAGS dedup cache. First prove native correctness after expiry and resurrection, then physical read/CPU effect; never apply to production.
next_action.stop_condition: If active sample output changes, old ID cannot resume, old backfills become visible incorrectly, or replay misses TimeRanges, reject cleanup design.
